children: were down by over 1% premarket on Friday after Morgan Stanley downgraded the drugmaker, saying that the overhang from the loss of exclusivity of semaglutide remains a key concern.

“The key issue of the investment case remains Novo's reliance on semaglutide (75% of sales in 2026e), which will face a large patent cliff in the early-mid 2030s across Europe and the US. We believe that the exposure to semaglutide will remain high at the start of the LOE impact from 2031 (we model 59% of sales in 2031),” the brokerage said and downgraded the stock to Underweight from Equal-weight.

Morgan Stanley analyst Thibault Boutherin forecasts Novo’s oral obesity franchise to reach $10 billion by 2031. However, the brokerage added that it is not expecting the obesity oral franchise to fully compensate for the headwinds faced by the company.

“The bulls may argue that oral formulation and new pipeline launches should ease the LOE impact, but we believe Novo's overall diabesity franchise will not be immune to the pricing pressure caused by generics versions of semaglutide, and we have concerns over the competitivity of its diabesity pipeline compared to Eli Lilly's and other branded pharma companies,” added Boutherin.

Going deeper, Morgan Stanley said the latest U.S. prescription data suggest a slowdown in Wegovy pill growth after a strong H1 '26 and that Eli Lilly's Zepbound has been capturing the majority of the bolus from Medicare patients since the start of the Bridge programme.

“While this could be transitory and seasonal, we see a credible risk that the slowdown is related to more structural factors,” it said, adding that the brokerage has "concerns over the competitivity of Novo's diabesity pipeline compared to Eli Lilly's and other branded pharma."
The Danish drugmaker and rival Eli Lilly

dominate the weight loss drug market. Each has their own injectable drugs—Novo's Wegovy (semaglutide) and Lilly's Zepbound (tirzepatide)—as well as oral drugs—a Wegovy pill from Novo and Foundayo (orforglipron). Follow-on drugs, such as Novo's CagriSema and Lilly's retatrutide, are also in development.

Overall, Novo Nordisk stock has fallen nearly 14% so far this year, compared to the roughly 11% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

title: Novo Nordisk falls as Morgan Stanley cuts rating to Underweight on semaglutide concern
